title: Derived internal Hom on a ringed site
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site whose underlying category is small and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$ (a ringed site); let $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ be its abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $D(\mathcal O)$ the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of $\Mod(\mathcal O)$, the localization of the category of cochain complexes of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] at the quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules]. For complexes $\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal M^\bullet$ of $\mathcal O$-modules, let $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal M^\bullet)$ be their Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex], with terms $\prod_{p\in\mathbf Z}\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal L^p,\mathcal M^{p+n})$ and differential $d(\varphi)=d_{\mathcal M}\circ\varphi-(-1)^n\varphi\circ d_{\mathcal L}$. Every complex $\mathcal M^\bullet$ has a K-injective resolution $\mathcal M^\bullet\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ [def-pur-kinjective-complex], which can be chosen functorially in $\mathcal M^\bullet$ [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; fix such a functorial choice $\mathcal M^\bullet\mapsto\mathcal I^\bullet(\mathcal M^\bullet)$. For $L,M\in D(\mathcal O)$, represented by complexes $\mathcal L^\bullet$ and $\mathcal M^\bullet$, the *derived internal Hom* is

$$
 R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(L,M)
 =\mathcal Hom^\bullet\bigl(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet(\mathcal M^\bullet)\bigr)\in D(\mathcal O).
$$

The assignment $(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal M^\bullet)\mapsto\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet(\mathcal M^\bullet))$ is a functor on pairs of complexes, contravariant in the first and covariant in the second variable; it sends a quasi-isomorphism in either variable to a quasi-isomorphism [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] (a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal M^\bullet\to(\mathcal M')^\bullet$ induces a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal I^\bullet(\mathcal M^\bullet)\to\mathcal I^\bullet((\mathcal M')^\bullet)$ of K-injective complexes, by the two-out-of-three property of quasi-isomorphisms). Hence, by the universal property of the localization, it induces a functor $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}:D(\mathcal O)^{\mathrm{op}}\times D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O)$. By the same lemma, the object obtained from any other K-injective complex $\mathcal I'^\bullet$ quasi-isomorphic to $\mathcal M^\bullet$ and any other representative of $L$ is canonically isomorphic to it.

proof.text: For a pair (t.op,s) of quasi-isomorphisms, naturality of eta and two-out-of-three show that I(s) is a quasi-isomorphism. Both I-targets are K-injective. Apply quasiIso_homComplex_mapMixedUniverses to I(s) and t, then DerivedCategory.isIso_Q_map_iff_quasiIso. This proves derivedInternalHomMixedUniverses_inverts and permits Localization.lift.

Use the source-library functorial K-injective resolution I0 and its map eta0 in the Grothendieck abelian module category. Localization.fac computes the lifted bifunctor on pairs of complexes. For an arbitrary replacement I, compare I0 and I through the composite M ↦ I(I0(M)): eta at I0(M) gives I0(M) to I(I0(M)), while I(eta0 at M) gives I(M) to I(I0(M)). Both are quasi-isomorphisms between K-injective targets, the latter by naturality and two-out-of-three. Applying Hom-complex followed by Q makes both natural transformations isomorphisms. Compose the factorization isomorphism with the first and the inverse of the second to prove derivedInternalHomMixedUniverses_comparison.

For a K-injective representative Ic, eta0 at Ic is a quasi-isomorphism between K-injective complexes. Applying Hom(Lc,-) and Q gives an isomorphism from Q Hom(Lc,Ic) to Q Hom(Lc,I0(Ic)). Evaluate the canonical comparison at (op Lc,Ic), compose with the inverse of this isomorphism, and transport along the given representative isomorphisms via derivedInternalHom.mapIso. This proves derivedInternalHomMixedUniverses_obj_iso without lifting any morphism from the derived category to a chain map.

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks sites-cohomology.tex Sections 0A8X, 08J7, 07A5, Lemmas 0A94/0A95/08JA, derived.tex Definition 070H and injectives.tex Theorem 079P (Lean state none on both branches). Named the notions the definition is built from: the sheaf-valued Hom complex (new def-pur-hom-complex, Stacks 0A8X, not in Mathlib: Mathlib's CochainComplex.HomComplex is group-valued), K-injective complexes and resolutions (new def-pur-kinjective-complex, Mathlib leaf CochainComplex.IsKInjective + QuasiIso over SheafOfModules), cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms of O-modules (existing Mathlib leaves def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules), Mod(O) (def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category) and D(O) (def-weil-abstract-derived-category). The two claims the definition needs became statement nodes: existence of functorial K-injective resolutions in Mod(O) (new prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist, Stacks 07A5 + 079P, not in Mathlib for unbounded complexes) and well-definedness/functoriality (new lem-pur-rhom-well-defined, Stacks 0A95). The statement now uses a fixed functorial choice of K-injective resolution, so that the functor D(O)^op x D(O) -> D(O) is defined, and assumes the site small (needed for Mod(O) to be Grothendieck abelian; Stacks' standing convention). The claim H^0(C, R Hom(L,M)) = Hom_D(L,M), a theorem rather than part of the definition, was removed from the statement and is the new node lem-pur-rhom-global-sections (Stacks 08JA), which depends on this one. def-pur-sheaf-hom is now reached through def-pur-hom-complex rather than directly.

lean.statement: def derivedInternalHomMixedUniverses {C : Type c} [Category.{v} C] (J : GrothendieckTopology C) [HasSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{max c v r}] [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{max c v r}] [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})] (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{r}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{max c v r} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj R))] : (DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max c v r} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj R)))ᵒᵖ × DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max c v r} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj R)) ⥤ DerivedCategory (SheafOfModules.{max c v r} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{r} RingCat.{r})).obj R))
lean.note: Section 1(B): derivedInternalHomOfUniverses requires the coefficient sheaf itself in max c v r. On the actual small etale site objects have universe u+1 and coefficient rings u. This companion uses the identical homComplexFunctor and localization construction, allowing rings in r and module sections in max c v r. It publicly re-exports the entire previous interface, including ordinaryModuleDerivedInternalHom and the comparison/independence APIs. No arbitrary bifunctor is chosen.
